title: Eastern Moghulistan
capsule: Eastern Moghulistan denotes the Turpan-based Chagatayid khanate that formed the eastern half of the divided Moghul realm after the 1514-16 split, ruled first by Mansur Khan (d. 1543) and then by his descendants from their oasis capital at Turpan and Qara Khoja. Squeezed between the rival Yarkent Khanate to the west and expanding Oirat power to the north, the Turpan line's authority steadily eroded, and most of its territory was absorbed by the Yarkent Khanate around 1570. The remaining Turpan Chagatayids survived as a diminished principality into the later seventeenth century until Dzungar expansion extinguished the line by the 1680s.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Moghulistan's territorial extent is reconstructed from Timurid chronicles, Chinese dynastic histories, and later Chagatai-language sources; the steppe frontiers were fluid and seasonal, and the polity's boundaries are broadly approximate rather than administratively demarcated. Capsule researched for this polity/era specifically (confidence: medium).
